title: Founding as the Cleveland Rams
content: The Rams were founded in 1936 in Cleveland, Ohio, and joined the NFL in 1937. As the Cleveland Rams they won the 1945 NFL Championship, beating Washington 15-14.

title: First move to Los Angeles
content: The team moved from Cleveland to Los Angeles in 1946, becoming the first major professional sports team on the West Coast. They played at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum until 1979, and won the 1951 NFL Championship there, beating the Cleveland Browns 24-17.

title: Years in Anaheim
content: From 1980 to 1994 the Rams played their home games at Anaheim Stadium. They reached Super Bowl XIV in January 1980 and lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers 31-19.

title: St. Louis era
content: The Rams moved to St. Louis in 1995 and played there through the 2015 season, mostly at the Trans World Dome (later the Edward Jones Dome). During that period they were known as the St. Louis Rams.

title: Return to Los Angeles
content: The Rams returned to Los Angeles in 2016. They played at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum from 2016 to 2019, then moved into SoFi Stadium in 2020.

title: Super Bowl XXXIV
content: The St. Louis Rams won Super Bowl XXXIV on January 30, 2000, beating the Tennessee Titans 23-16 in Atlanta. The game ended with linebacker Mike Jones tackling Kevin Dyson one yard short of the goal line. Quarterback Kurt Warner was named MVP.

title: Super Bowl LVI
content: The Los Angeles Rams won Super Bowl LVI on February 13, 2022, beating the Cincinnati Bengals 23-20 at SoFi Stadium. Wide receiver Cooper Kupp was named MVP. The Rams became the first team to win a Super Bowl in their own home stadium.

title: Championship and Super Bowl record
content: The Rams have won two Super Bowls (XXXIV and LVI) and two earlier NFL Championships (1945 and 1951). They have also lost three Super Bowls: XIV to the Steelers (1980), XXXVI to the Patriots 20-17 (2002), and LIII to the Patriots 13-3 (2019).

title: SoFi Stadium
content: The Rams play their home games at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, which opened in 2020. It seats about 70,000 and can expand to about 100,000 for major events. The Los Angeles Chargers share the stadium, and it hosted Super Bowl LVI.

title: League, division and colors
content: The Rams compete in the NFL's NFC West alongside the Arizona Cardinals, San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks. Their colors are royal blue and sol (yellow), their logo is a ram's horn, and their mascot is Rampage.

title: The Greatest Show on Turf
content: "The Greatest Show on Turf" was the Rams' high-scoring offense from 1999 to 2001. It featured quarterback Kurt Warner, running back Marshall Faulk, and receivers Isaac Bruce and Torry Holt, and the 1999 team scored 526 points on the way to the Super Bowl XXXIV title.

title: The Fearsome Foursome
content: The Fearsome Foursome was the Rams' dominant defensive line of the 1960s: Deacon Jones, Merlin Olsen, Rosey Grier and Lamar Lundy. Deacon Jones is credited with coining the term "sack".

title: Sean McVay
content: Sean McVay was hired as Rams head coach in January 2017 at age 30, the youngest head coach in modern NFL history. He has led the Rams to two Super Bowls, LIII and LVI, winning LVI.

title: Matthew Stafford
content: Matthew Stafford joined the Rams in 2021 in a trade with the Detroit Lions that sent Jared Goff and draft picks the other way. He quarterbacked the Rams to victory in Super Bowl LVI in his first season with the team.

title: Cooper Kupp
content: Cooper Kupp, a third-round pick from Eastern Washington in 2017, had a historic 2021 season: 145 receptions, 1,947 receiving yards and 16 touchdowns, leading the NFL in all three. He was named Offensive Player of the Year and Super Bowl LVI MVP.

title: Aaron Donald
content: Aaron Donald, a defensive tackle drafted 13th overall in 2014 out of Pittsburgh, won NFL Defensive Player of the Year three times (2017, 2018 and 2020) and was a key part of the Super Bowl LVI win. He retired in March 2024.

title: Eric Dickerson
content: Eric Dickerson rushed for 2,105 yards with the Rams in 1984, still the NFL single-season rushing record. He is in the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

title: Hall of Famers
content: Pro Football Hall of Famers who played for the Rams include Bob Waterfield, Norm Van Brocklin, Elroy "Crazylegs" Hirsch, Tom Fears, Deacon Jones, Merlin Olsen, Jack Youngblood, Eric Dickerson, Orlando Pace, Kurt Warner, Marshall Faulk and Isaac Bruce.

title: Super Bowl LIII loss
content: The Los Angeles Rams lost Super Bowl LIII to the New England Patriots 13-3 on February 3, 2019, in Atlanta. It was the lowest-scoring Super Bowl in history.

title: Super Bowl XXXVI loss
content: The St. Louis Rams lost Super Bowl XXXVI to the New England Patriots 20-17 on February 3, 2002, in New Orleans, on a last-second field goal by Adam Vinatieri.

title: Every home stadium in Rams history
content: The Rams have played their home games in Cleveland (1936-1945), at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum (1946-1979), at Anaheim Stadium (1980-1994), at the Trans World Dome / Edward Jones Dome in St. Louis (1995-2015), back at the Coliseum (2016-2019), and at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood since 2020.
